The snpscape object

Source: R/snpscape.R
snpscape.Rd

A snpscape object holds everything snpscaper knows about a set of genotypes. It is created by fetch_region() and passed along to the other functions. Printing it gives a short summary.

Details

It is a list with four parts:

  • genotypes: a matrix with one row per person and one column per SNP. Each value is the number of copies of the alternative allele that the person carries (0, 1 or 2), or NA if unknown.

  • variants: a tibble describing each SNP (one row per column of genotypes): id, chrom, pos (position on GRCh38), ref (reference allele), alt (alternative allele), region (which requested region it came from) and rsid (rs number, for well-known SNPs only).

  • samples: a tibble describing each person (one row per row of genotypes); see samples_1kg.

  • provenance: where the data came from and what has been done to them: the regions fetched, genome build, data source, date, package version and a log of filtering steps.

You rarely need to touch these parts directly, but you can, e.g. x$samples or x$variants.
